Authors: Ruonan Yi, Jia Yan, Debo Shi, Yu-Tong Tian, Fei-Yue Chen, Zi-Jian Wang, Shu-Kai Duan
Title: Improving the performance of drifted/shifted electronic nose systems by cross-domain transfer using common transfer samples
Abstract: Abstract Sensor drift/shift is a challenging and high-profile issue in the field of sensors and measurements. Because of the time variability and unpredictable properties of drift/shift, traditional compensation methods are costly and laborious. Considering the distribution alignments of different domains at both the feature and decision level, a unified double-level drift/shift compensation framework is presented to address sensor drift/shift. The framework consists of cross-domain feature subspace transfer learning coupled with a cross-domain adaptation extreme learning machine (CFST-AELM), which learns a low-dimensional discriminant subspace and a robust classifier using small numbers of labeled samples selected from the target domain. In general, the unified framework has the following advantages: (1) implementing anti-drift/shift at both the feature and decision level by cross-domain transfer learning which takes full advantage of transfer samples; (2) the subspace learning is a joint distribution adaptation algorithm and can be easily realized by eigenvalue decomposition; (3) more discriminative information of the source and target datasets remain after linear mapping; and (4) there is enhancement of the generalization performance of the model by adding the prediction error of transfer samples as a constraint of extreme learning machines (ELM) classification. The results suggest that compared with several state-of-the-art strategies, the CFST-AELM framework has superior performance in terms of classification accuracy.

Authors: Bei Liu, Xiao-Ping Zeng, Fengchun Tian, Shuya Zhang, Leilei Zhao
Title: Domain Transfer Broad Learning System for Long-Term Drift Compensation in Electronic Nose Systems
Abstract: The long-term sensor drift phenomenon seriously restricts the performance of Electronic Nose (E-nose) systems in their various applications. Due to frequent recalibrations, traditional drift compensation methods are costly and laborious, and their performance are limited due to the nonlinear dynamic properties of the drift. The latest proposed Broad Learning System (BLS) has been confirmed to be an efficient and effective learning technique for many machine learning problems. However, BLS with cross-domain learning capability has rarely been studied. In this paper, a novel unified framework called Domain Transfer Broad Learning System (DTBLS) is proposed based on BLS, to address the issue of drift via adaptive compensation. For the case where there is no labeled target sample, with simultaneous considerations of the empirical loss of source data, marginal distribution adaptation, conditional distribution adaptation and manifold regularization, the DTBLS framework learns a robust target classifier by using labeled source data and unlabeled target data to compensate the drift of sensor response adaptively. To the best of our knowledge, DTBLS is the first BLS-based transfer learning framework for the problem of dataset shift existing in E-nose systems. Like the basic BLS, high computation efficiency is achieved due to the existence of analytical solution. Parameter sensitivity analysis is also conducted to show that the optimal solution can be obtained in a wide range. Experiments on a public gas sensor drift dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods well.

Authors: Chung-Yen Lee, Pang-Chun Liu, Shih-Wen Chiu, Kea-Tiong Tang
Title: CycleGAN-based Domain Smoothing for Stable Adversarial Adaptation (CDS-AA)
Source: 2026 IEEE International Symposium on Olfaction and Electronic Nose (ISOEN)
Abstract: Aging in electronic-nose sensors induces batch-wise distribution drift, severely degrading cross-batch classification accuracy. To address this problem, we propose a drift-compensation framework that combines 1D CycleGAN-based pseudo-domain generation [1], [3], Domain-Adversarial Neural Networks (DANN) [2], and a support vector machine (SVM) ensemble. Three pair-specific CycleGAN mappings are first learned from the shared classes (2–4) and then applied to source-domain unseen gases (5–6) to generate pseudo target representations. These pseudo samples are used for downstream classification and adversarial alignment, while real target samples of gases 5–6 remain unlabeled during training. In this framework, CycleGAN captures transferable batch-shift geometry from shared classes, whereas DANN further aligns pseudo and real target feature distributions to improve robustness. Experiments on three representative drift scenarios—severe drift with sparse shared data (1→6), moderate and coherent drift $(\mathbf{6} \rightarrow \mathbf{1 0})$, and highly nonlinear drift with the lowest baseline accuracy $(\mathbf{9} \rightarrow \mathbf{1 0})$—show that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional baselines. In the most challenging $\mathbf{9} \rightarrow \mathbf{1 0}$ case, baseline SVM achieves only 20.33% accuracy, whereas the proposed method reaches $\mathbf{8 5}-\mathbf{8 8} \boldsymbol{\%}$. These results indicate that drift geometry extracted from shared classes provides transferable structure for compensating unseen-gas drift and substantially improves cross-batch classification robustness in MOX-based electronicnose systems [4]–[6].
